title: introduce cross-session affinity microbatch replay and compact delta serializer
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: We frequently see run-to-run variance from cross-session interference and microburst alignment when replaying production traces. This PR adds a new runner and an associated compact reporting pipeline to (1) reproduce steady-state microbatching behavior across sessions by grouping requests with token-affinity heuristics, and (2) emit a compact delta-serialized telemetry stream suitable for long-term per-kernel occupancy analysis.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Implements a Cross-Session Affinity Microbatch Replay runner that uses a time-windowed "turnstile" packer to form microbatches across session boundaries, an adaptive jitter mechanism to avoid synchronized batching spikes, and a delta-serializer output that compresses repetitive telemetry records between iterations. The runner ships with a lightweight kernel-occupancy mapper that folds GPU-side slot attribution into compact heatmap tiles.

Design highlights and trade-offs:
- Affinity metric: token-sequence fingerprinting (fast, low-cost hash) used to prefer co-location in microbatches; this favors cache reuse but can increase cold-priming for rare prefixes.
- Turnstile window: bounded (configurable 5-50ms) to balance latency realism and batch packing rate.
- Jitter scheduler: small randomized offsets prevent pathological alignment across simultaneous session replays.
- Delta serializer: protobuf-ish compact format (binary) that stores only changed fields per-report to reduce long-run telemetry size; integrated with existing benchmark-lab reporters.
- Backpressure simulation: the runner can inject kernel-level backpressure events to exercise slow-path scheduling and observe occupancy drop/recovery.

Files changed (high level):
- benchmark-lab/runners/affinity_microbatch_run.py: new runner (core logic, config)
- benchmark-lab/packers/turnstile_packer.py: turnstile window and jitter logic
- benchmark-lab/reporters/delta_serializer.go: compact delta serialization for telemetry export (binary)
- benchmark-lab/reporters/occupancy_mapper.py: heatmap tile generator and per-kernel slot attribution
- benchmark-lab/tests/test_affinity_replay.py: unit + integration tests for deterministic replay modes
- benchmark-lab/configs/affinity-defaults.yaml: default knobs for experiments
- docs/benchmarks/affinity-runbook.md: how to run and interpret outputs

Testing and validation performed:
- Unit tests: packer/jitter/serializer correctness vectors added.
- Local integration: replayed a 30k-session production-derived trace in local-mini-cluster and validated no regressions in runner liveness.
- Perf baseline: compared legacy single-session replayer vs new cross-session microbatch on an rtx-8x node with a representative multi-tenant trace: p95 latency decreased 12% under sustained load; mean GPU active time improved by ~8%; telemetry payloads reduced by ~65% storage when using delta-serializer on 1M events.
- Stability: exercised runner for 24h continuous run with periodic backpressure injections — no memory leaks, KV cache hit rate stable.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement runner and packer
- [x] Add deterministic unit and integration tests
- [x] Add basic docs and runbook
- [x] Add CI bench job that validates smoke metrics
- [x] Wire up delta-serializer to existing reporters
- [x] Performance measurements recorded and attached

How to run (quick): 
1) python -m benchmark_lab.runners.affinity_microbatch_run --trace traces/prod-30k.json --config configs/affinity-defaults.yaml --emit=delta_stream.bin
2) go run benchmark-lab/reporters/delta_serializer.go decode --in delta_stream.bin --out decoded/ --compact-heatmap=decoded/heatmap.tgz
3) Use docs/benchmarks/affinity-runbook.md to interpret heatmap tiles and per-kernel slot traces.

Open items / follow-ups: 
- Integrate delta-serializer as a sink for long-term S3 archival with a CLI tool for index creation (ENG-1350).
- Tune affinity hashing for longer prefix reuse; could be gated behind a config knob for high-variance workloads.

Why this is different: Existing runners primarily replay within single-session or simple interleaving; this PR explicitly targets cross-session microbatching effects and provides a space-efficient telemetry export designed for long-running baseline collection, making it practical to keep high-fidelity per-kernel occupancy history for regression detection.

feat(run): add affinity microbatch replay runner
feat(packer): implement turnstile window and jitter scheduler

review_thread:
Evan Chen: Can you make the affinity hashing pluggable? Some traces may benefit from token-weighted fingerprints.
Priya (author): Good call — added a simple hashing interface and a default implementation; added tests to verify swap-in.
Aisha Raman: The jitter parameters look potentially risky for latency-sensitive experiments; can we make it opt-in per config?
Priya: Jitter is configurable (defaults small); docs updated to call out when to disable.
Tomás López: CI bench flaked once on memory pressure; suggested adding a small heap assertion after long runs.
Priya: Added a regression test that asserts resident size growth and re-ran 24h smoke locally.
Approvals: Evan Chen — approved, Aisha Raman — approved after changes, Tomás López — approved.

release_notes: Introduce cross-session affinity microbatch replay runner and compact delta serializer. Adds a new toolset for reproducing microbatch alignment and generating compressed per-kernel occupancy telemetry for long-term regression tracking. Performance: reduced p95 by ~12% in representative runs and decreased telemetry storage by ~65% on sampled workloads.
